top.line: Three LinkedIn pages drafted in the open
top.para: sgit.ai, the SGit Newsroom and RiskMandate have no LinkedIn pages. The agent gathered LinkedIn's requirements and drafted each page, thirty first posts and a new profile, published openly because the site documents the story. The addresses looked free, the newsroom gets a company page, and RiskMandate's is agreed with the co-founder.

in-short.line: Free addresses, drafted fields, thirty posts, a profile
in-short.para: Three active companies have no pages; this is done in the open. The addresses returned 404 on 18 October. The newsroom gets a company page because a showcase page cannot be an employer. Every field is drafted with its count, thirty first posts are already published, and the profile is new.

why.line: The site documents the story, including this
why.para: The site captures what is actually happening, including work usually done quietly. Newsroom subscribers follow exactly this, so the drafts are published before they are done rather than appearing finished later.

decide.line: Addresses, page type, relations and requirements
decide.para: The three addresses returned 404 without logging in. Showcase pages cannot be employers, have jobs, or show in search to non-followers, so the newsroom gets a company page. The three pages list each other as affiliated, with The Cyber Boardroom as the entity. LinkedIn's requirements and the limits used, and their sources, are listed.

sgit.para: Software Development, 1 to 10, privately held. The tagline and about describe client-side encrypted vaults, read and write keys, append lanes, the open-source CLI, web app and storage, the paid service through sgraph.ai, beta status and published vaults. Ten first posts run from why sgit to a vault on Cloudflare.

newsroom.line: The SGit Newsroom: written in the open
newsroom.para: Online Media, 1 to 10, privately held. The about covers voice memos turned into sourced, versioned articles by named agents, pay-after-you-read, more than 180 articles, four beta wires, a newsletter and reviews on the record. The six issues are already a LinkedIn newsletter. Ten first posts are listed.

riskmandate.para: Computer and Network Security, 1 to 10, privately held, agreed with the co-founder first. The about explains reach, mandate, gap and barriers, staying out of the request path, one-time prices from £10 to £1,500, sixteen free templates and the open vocabulary, and not being an insurer. Ten first posts are listed.

profile.line: A new headline, about and two bios
profile.para: A 152-character headline naming the three companies, encrypted vaults, behaviour policies and the OWASP Board; an about tying the companies to thirty years in security, OWASP work and ten books; a 50-word and a 130-word bio; and experience entries linked to the new pages.

limits.line: Drafts, unverified limits, details to confirm
limits.para: None of the pages exists yet, and a free address does not prove no page exists elsewhere. Some limits come from LinkedIn Learning, blogs and guides, not help pages. Founding years and locations are not on the sites, and RiskMandate's text awaits the co-founder.

sources.line: LinkedIn's help pages and the companies' sites
sources.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026, LinkedIn's help pages on creating pages, eligibility, showcase pages, images, newsletters and industry codes, read that day, and the companies' own sites and this site's about, ids and shipped pages.
